# Actor CSV export is lossy — AKA and tag round-trip

> Data-fidelity defect in the actor CSV export/import. The export omitted fields the library actively curates, so a CSV was a lossy representation of the catalogue and a round-trip silently discarded user data. **Status: IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-02.** Shipped in `ed25942`; verified against the live 1,336-actor library. See the Delivery record at the foot of this page.
## Intention
Make the actor CSV a faithful representation of an actor profile, so that exporting and re-importing preserves what the user has curated — and so that any external tool consuming the export can see the fields that matter for identity.
## The defect
`EntityProfile` stores several collection fields that the CSV format cannot represent:
| Field | Exported? | Imported? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `akas` (pseudonyms / also-known-as) | ❌ no column | ❌ `akas: existing?.akas ?? []` |
| `tags` | ❌ no column | ❌ `tags: existing?.tags ?? []` |
| `galleryUrls` | ❌ no column | ❌ `galleryUrls: existing?.galleryUrls ?? []` |
**Export** — `ActorGridView.swift:607` writes a nine-column header:
```javascript
Name,Bio,PhotoURL,HomePage,Gender,HairColor,BirthYear,CountryOfOrigin,Rating
```
**Import** — `ActorGridView.swift:713-715` rebuilds each profile with the collection fields copied from the *existing* record, never read from the file.
The import behaviour is deliberate and correct **given** the format: since the CSV cannot carry these fields, preserving them is the only safe choice, and this specifically guards the data-loss bug class recorded as C3 in the defect inventory. **The defect is in the format, not the guard.**
### Why AKAs matter most
The AKA list is the mechanism by which **multiple names are associated with a single actor profile** — performers work under pseudonyms, and the library models that today. Omitting AKAs from the export means:
- **A round-trip is lossy in the user's mental model.** "Export, edit in Numbers, re-import" is a documented workflow (see in-app Help). A user reasonably expects the file to represent the actor.
- **External tooling is blind to identity.** Any tool consuming the export sees only the primary name, so it cannot tell that two names denote one actor — and may propose creating a duplicate profile for a pseudonym.
- **It is the strongest identity signal the library holds**, and it is the one thing the format drops.
## Design
### Add an AKA column
Append at the next free index — **never insert**, and never reorder. `importCSV` reads `columns[0..8]` **positionally** and ignores the header row entirely, so inserting a column would silently misfile every value after it (a bio would land in `homePage`). Column 0 is the identity key: rewriting it creates a new actor rather than updating one.
> ⚠️ **Coordinate the index.** Other planned work also appends columns. Whichever lands first takes the lower indices; the second must rebase rather than assume a position. The importer's `columns.count >= 4` guard must rise as columns are wired up.
### Delimiter
> ✅ **RESOLVED in D1 below — pipe.** The options are retained for history.
❓ *(superseded)* AKAs are a list inside one cell. Two candidates:
- **Pipe-delimited** (`Jane Doe|J. Doe`) — unambiguous, survives naive spreadsheet editing, no interaction with CSV quoting. Recommended.
- **Comma-delimited inside a quoted cell** — consistent with how `HairColor` already carries multiple values, but relies on `escapeCSV` quoting and is easy for a user to break by hand in a spreadsheet.
Whichever is chosen must round-trip an AKA that itself contains the delimiter, or reject it explicitly.
### Scope — which fields?
> ✅ **RESOLVED in D2 below — AKAs and tags in, gallery URLs out.** Retained for history; note the tag-normalisation objection was withdrawn.
❓ *(superseded)* AKAs alone, or also `tags` and `galleryUrls`?
- **AKAs alone** — smallest change, fixes the identity gap, one column.
- **All three** — makes the CSV genuinely faithful, but `galleryUrls` can be long and `tags` may be numerous, producing unwieldy cells. Tags additionally interact with the tag taxonomy: an import that writes tags could introduce near-duplicate tags that `TagNormalizer` would otherwise have caught.
Recommendation: **AKAs now**, tags and gallery URLs assessed separately — they raise normalisation questions that AKAs do not.
### Merge semantics
Consistent with the existing non-destructive import contract:
- A **blank** AKA cell leaves the existing list untouched — it must never clear curated AKAs.
- A **populated** cell must specify union-with-existing or replace. ✅ **RESOLVED in D3 — union with dedup.**
- Duplicate entries are de-duplicated; ordering is not significant.
- An AKA identical to the primary `Name` is dropped rather than stored.
## Decisions — Human Operator (resolved)
### ✅ D1 — Delimiter: pipe (`|`)
`Jane Doe|J. Doe`. Chosen to **avoid quoting entirely**. A stage name can legitimately contain a comma ("Smith, Jr."), which would be ambiguous inside a comma-delimited cell and depends on quote handling surviving a hand-edit in a spreadsheet. A pipe never appears in a name.
JSON-in-cell was rejected: faithful to storage, hostile to the documented "export, edit in Numbers, re-import" workflow.
A value containing a literal `|` must round-trip correctly or be rejected explicitly — never silently split.
### ✅ D2 — Scope: AKAs **and** tags. Gallery URLs excluded.
**Tags are IN.** The original objection was normalisation risk — a CSV import writing tags could introduce near-duplicates that `TagNormalizer` would otherwise catch. That objection is void: the tags UI offers a pick-list of existing tags, which has kept the vocabulary under ~30 in practice. No extra processing is required.
**Gallery URLs are OUT.** Rationale (Human Operator): *they carry no identifying information.* Identity is precisely what this fix exists to restore. They are also bulk reference data — many long URLs per actor would produce unwieldy cells — and `.actorpkg` already provides full-fidelity actor transfer including the actual image bytes, which a CSV can never do. The CSV's job is the text metadata that gets hand-edited.
> **⚠️ Consequence for the enrichment spec.** D7 of *Actor Metadata Enrichment* states that tag enrichment is structurally impossible through the CSV path, which is why the `Redhead` and ethnicity tag rules were Phase-3-only. **Once this lands, that is no longer true** — the batch path can apply tags across all matched actors instead of one at a time in the app. D7 must be amended when this ships.
### ✅ D3 — Merge: union with existing, de-duplicated
Worked example from the Human Operator: existing `{John, Jon}` merged with incoming `{John, Jonathan}` yields `John | Jon | Jonathan`.
- A **blank** cell leaves the existing list untouched — never clears.
- A **populated** cell is unioned with the existing list, not substituted.
- Duplicates are removed; ordering is not significant.
- An entry identical to the primary `Name` is dropped rather than stored.
**Accepted trade-off:** an AKA or tag cannot be *removed* through the CSV — removal stays an in-app action. Chosen deliberately: replace-semantics would turn a truncated or mistakenly-cleared cell into silent data loss, which is the worse failure mode for a fix whose entire purpose is preventing data loss.
### ✅ D4 — Column indices (coordination)
The importer reads **positionally**, so index assignment is a contract, not a detail:
```javascript
0 Name          3 HomePage    6 BirthYear         9  AKAs
1 Bio           4 Gender      7 CountryOfOrigin   10 Tags
2 PhotoURL      5 HairColor   8 Rating
```
This work claims **9 (AKAs)** and **10 (Tags)**. The *Actor Metadata Enrichment* spec's additive columns therefore shift to **11–15** (`CareerSpan`, `CareerStart`, `CareerEnd`, `AgeAtCareerStart`, `BirthDate`). Whichever ships second rebases; it must never assume a position.
## Acceptance criteria
- Export includes an **AKAs** column (index 9) populated from `EntityProfile.akas`, pipe-delimited.
- Export includes a **Tags** column (index 10) populated from `EntityProfile.tags`, pipe-delimited.
- Import reads both and applies union-with-dedup semantics.
- `galleryUrls` remains preserved-from-existing and is **not** represented in the CSV.
- A value containing a literal `|` round-trips correctly or is rejected explicitly — never silently split.
- An AKA or tag equal to the primary `Name` is dropped rather than stored.
- **Round-trip fidelity:** export → import with no edits leaves every actor's AKA list byte-identical. Asserted for a library containing actors with zero, one, and many AKAs.
- A blank AKA cell never clears an existing list.
- Existing nine-column CSVs (produced before this change) still import correctly — the new column is optional, and its absence is not an error.
- A reordered or renamed header is **rejected** rather than silently misread.
- Column 0 is never rewritten by any import path.
- No regression to the C3 guard: a throwing profile fetch must still abort the import rather than proceed with empty collections.
## Test strategy
Characterization first, per personal standards — capture current export/import behaviour before changing it, and keep those tests passing.
- **Round-trip** with 0 / 1 / many AKAs, including names containing commas, quotes, and the chosen delimiter.
- **Backward compatibility** — a nine-column file from the previous version imports without error.
- **Blank-cell preservation** — the existing list survives.
- **Failure states** — malformed row, delimiter inside a value, duplicate AKAs, an AKA equal to the primary name, and a row whose column count falls below the guard.
- **No behaviour change in a refactor commit**, per personal standards.
## Open decisions — Human Operator
- ✅ **Delimiter** — resolved: pipe. See D1.
- ✅ **Scope** — resolved: AKAs and tags in, gallery URLs out. See D2.
- ✅ **Merge semantics** — resolved: union with dedup. See D3.
- ✅ **Column indices** — resolved: AKAs at 9, Tags at 10. See D4.
*All open decisions are closed. This specification is ready for approval.*
## Delivery record — IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-02
Shipped in commit `ed25942`. GitHub: [#11](https://github.com/mranlett/ViLM/issues/11) (closed), plus [#12](https://github.com/mranlett/ViLM/issues/12) raised and fixed along the way.
### What shipped
- **Format extracted to ****`LibraryCore/ActorCSV.swift`** — it previously lived inside a SwiftUI view and could not be tested at all. The two country transforms are injected, since `CountryFlagHelper` is app-target-only.
- **AKAs at index 9, Tags at index 10**, pipe-delimited, with backslash escaping so a literal `|` round-trips instead of splitting.
- **Union-with-dedup on import**, case-insensitive, existing casing preserved, entries equal to the primary name dropped on both export and import so a no-edit round trip is stable.
- **Header validation** — `importCSV` now rejects a reordered, renamed or headerless file naming the offending column, while still accepting nine-column legacy files, extra trailing columns, case differences, surrounding whitespace and a BOM.
- **Zero-row imports now report an error** rather than succeeding silently.
- **44 tests** in `ActorCSVTests`; 360 across `LibraryCore`.
### Verified in production (1,346 videos / 1,339 actors, iPhone 16 Pro Max)
- Export: 1,336 rows, all 11 columns, no ragged rows. **All nine original columns byte-identical in fill rate**, proving the extraction changed nothing.
- Import: AKAs and tags merged into real profiles.
- Invariants held on real data — zero self-referential AKAs, zero duplicates.
### ⚠️ Defect discovered during implementation — #12
Writing the characterization tests exposed a latent bug: **Swift treats ****`\r\n`**** as a SINGLE Character**, so the parser's `char == "\n" || char == "\r"` never matched a Windows line ending. A CRLF file collapsed into one row, `dropFirst()` discarded it, and **the import silently did nothing**.
It then hit the Human Operator in production on the first real round trip — an edited file, saved by a spreadsheet editor as CRLF, imported zero of 1,336 rows while reporting success. Proven on the actual file:
```javascript
BEFORE (literal comparison)     AFTER (isNewline)
  parsed rows      : 1            parsed rows      : 1337
  after dropFirst(): 0            after dropFirst(): 1336
```
Fixed by testing `Character.isNewline`, and paired with the zero-row error so the same class of silent failure cannot recur unseen.
### Residual
The **reordered-header rejection** is unit-tested (nine cases) and wired, but has never been exercised on device by feeding the app a deliberately scrambled CSV. Low risk, recorded for completeness.
### Consequence for the enrichment spec
D2 here put **tags into the CSV**, which supersedes D7 of *Actor Metadata Enrichment*: tag enrichment is no longer Phase-3-only, so the batch path can now apply `Redhead` and ethnicity tags across all matched actors.
---
## Evidence
`ActorGridView.swift:607` (export header), `:678-720` (positional import), `:713-715` (collection fields preserved, not read). `EntityProfile.swift` (`akas`, `tags`, `galleryUrls`). In-app Help text already tells users that tags, gallery photos and aliases are preserved because "this format doesn't carry them" — the behaviour is documented, but the omission is still a fidelity gap. Defect-inventory context: C3 (the `try?`-fetch-then-save wipe, since fixed) and M4 (row-by-row saves, since made transactional).
